name: Facet
text: Ship a real-time contrast checker that overlays the dark theme’s text and background directly in the interface. This forces the team to fix contrast issues before submission, cutting rework and ensuring visibility. The trade-off is a slight slowdown in editing speed, but clarity and enjoyment for users outweigh it.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk is training users to ignore the contrast problem—once they see the c | overlay flicker, they’ll learn to tolerate it, not fix it. A pre-submission block risks drop-off; a live checker risks habituation. Settle it with A/B testing: half the users get the overlay, half get a hard block at submission—measure both drop-off and post-submission fixes.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-submission contrast blocker. It stops bad contrast from ever reaching users, guaranteeing visibility and enjoyment for everyone. The trade-off is a brief slowdown for submitters, but that’s a one-time cost for permanent quality. A hard block forces fixes upfront; overlays train tolerance.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A pre-submission block still trains users to dread the block—once they hit it, they’ll game the system, not learn contrast. Instead, ship a live contrast score in the sidebar that updates as they edit; users fix issues in the moment without interruption. Settle it with A/B testing: half see the score, half see the blocker—measure drop-off and fix rates.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship a live contrast score in the sidebar that updates in real-time, paired with a non-blocking, self-clearing warning overlay for immediate fixes—no pre-submission block, no flicker habituation. The result must deliver a clear, enjoyable interface that trains users to value contrast without interruption. Own it: Facet.
